content: If your doctor has prescribed low-dose aspirin (typically 81–162 milligrams per day) to prevent heart attack or stroke, you should continue taking it unless instructed otherwise by your doctor. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, while Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as monitoring sodium levels, as recommended by your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not freeze it or store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, be aware that it may contain sugar, which requires caution if you have diabetes. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This information was last revised in May 2024.
